provenance.subject: the two halves of the drift stop, which have DIFFERENT mechanisms and must not be conflated
provenance.design_reference: docs/aben-design.md section 9 final bullet, and section 6's determinism-and-races paragraph; alice's acceptance amendment of 2026-08-14 resolving this in the critic's favour

half_one_double_compute.property: within ONE prepare: registry observations captured ONCE, the patch computed TWICE from the same captured observations and SHAs, byte-identical output required
half_one_double_compute.mechanism: a deliberately nondeterministic resolver stub must trigger the within-invocation double-compute refusal
half_one_double_compute.why_no_data_here: this half is a pure nondeterminism detector over IDENTICAL captured inputs. It is triggered by a resolver seam, not by any registry state - release-dev reports it is already built and tested in scripts/release_normalizer_run.py. A data fixture cannot express it: the whole point is that the DATA does not change while the OUTPUT does. Authoring registry data for this half would test something else and look like coverage.
half_one_double_compute.history_worth_keeping: alice's original wording was 'normalizer output changed between two runs with no intervening commit'. That was amended to FROM IDENTICAL CAPTURED INPUTS because the literal between-two-runs form would have required persisted state - growing the plan-state class back through an acceptance criterion - and it conflated nondeterminism with registry races. The amendment is why this file has two halves instead of one.

half_two_exit_reobservation.property: load-bearing registry facts are re-observed immediately before leaving the cheap phase; if the world moved, the stop is under its REAL name
half_two_exit_reobservation.expected_stop: version-occupied (or registry-conflict, per which fact moved) - named, never a generic drift code
half_two_exit_reobservation.data: the two snapshots above are the pair: at capture, pypi:awid-service serves 0.5.15 only, so 0.5.16 is free and the normalizer intends to move there; at the exit re-observation, 0.5.16 has become occupied. The intended target was taken by someone else mid-invocation.
half_two_exit_reobservation.why_this_half_IS_data: unlike half one, here the captured input genuinely differs between the two reads. That is a registry race, it is representable as two recorded worlds, and this pair is the minimal one - a single member, a single version appearing.
half_two_exit_reobservation.discriminating_control: the same pair with the second snapshot IDENTICAL to the first must NOT stop. If the mechanism stops on an unchanged re-observation it is not detecting movement, and a green on the moving pair would prove nothing.

construction.warning: The 0.5.16-appears-mid-invocation event is counterfactual - no such race was recorded. The anchor SHA is real and re-observed (git rev-list -1 awid-service-v0.5.15 = 41008e6cb236c473546e84bd46660a9c852b264a, observed 2026-08-14 by aben-dev2), and 0.5.16 is a real version that really was published later, which is what makes the counterfactual a plausible race rather than an arbitrary one.
construction.note: shape follows release-dev's CapturedWorld registry half, with the second world under exit_reobservation so that one file carries the pair. If R6 prefers two sibling files, splitting is mechanical and the provenance travels with them.
